question: What's the PSI in Tampines right now?
name: Claude
answer:
Tampines is in Singapore's **East** region, and the haze there is at an **unhealthy** level.

**Latest reading I found (17 Oct, 8:30pm, NEA data via healthscreening.sg):**
- **24-hour PSI (East): 178, "Unhealthy"** (the unhealthy range is 101–200)
- **1-hour PM2.5 (East): 116 µg/m³, Band II "Elevated"**

**How it changed today:**
- At 2pm the East's 24-hour PSI was 173, and its 1-hour PM2.5 was 159, in the "High" band (The Star).
- On 16 Oct the East reached "very unhealthy" (205 around noon). It has dropped back into the unhealthy range since then.
- For 17 Oct, NEA forecast a PSI of 150–230, which spans "unhealthy" to "very unhealthy."

The 24-hour PSI is an average over the past day, so it changes slowly. The 1-hour PM2.5 figure gives a better sense of the air outside right now. Readings update every hour, so for the newest number, check NEA's site (haze.gov.sg) or the myENV app.

**While the PSI is unhealthy,** everyone should cut back on long or strenuous outdoor activity. Children, older people, pregnant women and anyone with heart or lung conditions should avoid it, and N95 masks help if you need to be outside for a long time.

SINGAPORE; Hazy conditions persisted into the afternoon of Oct 17, even as the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) in central Singapore dipped back into the “unhealthy” band after remaining in the “very unhealthy” range the previous day.

# Singapore haze keeps air quality unhealthy across island, with PM2.5 levels high in most regions
SINGAPORE; Hazy conditions persisted into the afternoon of Oct 17, even as the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) in central Singapore dipped back into the “unhealthy” band after remaining in the “very unhealthy” range the previous day.

At 2pm, the 24-hour PSI was in the “unhealthy” range in all regions: central (184), north (135), south (154), east (173) and west (185).

Meanwhile, hourly PM2.5 readings entered the “high” range in the west at 158 at 11am, followed by the central and southern regions at noon and the east at 2pm.



At 2pm, hourly PM2.5 readings stood at 243 in the west, 179 in the central region, 162 in the south and 159 in the east. The figure remained in the “elevated” range in the north at 91.

Air quality is considered “unhealthy” when the PSI – a 24-hour rolling average of six key air pollutants – is between 101 and 200, and “very unhealthy” when it is between 201 and 300.

Hourly PM2.5 readings are measured in micrograms per cubic metre and used as an indicator of current air quality.

In its daily haze advisory on the evening of Oct 16, the National Environment Agency (NEA) said the PSI forecast for Oct 17 could range from 150 to 230, putting air quality in the “unhealthy” to “very unhealthy” categories.
